g.text: An editorial overview of the archipelago’s geography, macroeconomic trajectory, demographics, and cultural landscape.
東アジアの島国 • 伝統と最先端技術の融合
Japan is an east Asian archipelago comprising 6,852 islands,
anchored by five principal landmasses: Honshu, Hokkaido,
Kyushu, Shikoku, and Okinawa. Extending across the volcanic
Pacific Ring of Fire, nearly three-quarters of its terrain is
mountainous and heavily forested, concentrating its dynamic
urban population along fertile coastal plains.
A NATION AT THE CROSSROADS OF TRADITION AND INNOVATION
"Japan pairs ancestral reverence with futuristic infrastructure—from centuries-old wooden shrines to the Shinkansen bullet train network."

Renowned for exemplary public safety, pioneering robotics, high life expectancy, and cultural soft power spanning cuisine to digital animation, Japan continues to adapt its economic model to an evolving demographic landscape while maintaining an indispensable role in international trade, advanced manufacturing, and regional diplomacy.
世界第4位の経済大国 • 円相場と名目GDP
Japan maintains the world’s fourth-largest economy by
nominal GDP, recognized for unparalleled industrial precision,
semiconductor materials, precision robotics, and cutting-edge

to over ¥155/$), rather than a collapse in real domestic output,
even as corporate revenues and the Nikkei touched record peaks.

*Note: Japan remains one of the OECD's most homogeneous nations; expanded technical visa pathways have increased foreign residency to record levels.
Six essential cultural, historical, and geographic milestones across the country
A kinetic metropolis where cutting-edge skyscrapers and neon scramble crossings coexist with tranquil Meiji shrine gardens and Michelin dining.
Over a thousand years of imperial history preserved in 2,000 Buddhist temples, Zen gardens, Fushimi Inari’s torii corridor, and historic Gion.
Celebrated for its warm, convivial spirit, towering 16th-century Osaka Castle, neon-lit Dotonbori canals, and vibrant street cuisine (takoyaki).
A moving testament to world peace at the Memorial Park, complemented by Itsukushima Shrine’s ethereal floating vermilion torii gate.
Japan’s iconic 3,776-meter stratovolcano, paired with Hakone’s mineral-rich hot spring baths, Lake Ashi pirate ships, and artisan ryokans.
A vast outdoor sanctuary of world-class powder snow in Niseko, summer lavender fields in Furano, pristine national parks, and fresh seafood.

DATA SOURCES: International Monetary Fund (IMF) World Economic Outlook (Current USD GDP) • Statistics Bureau, Ministry of Internal Affairs & Communications • Immigration Services Agency of Japan (MOJ).
